sn19.10:1.1: The “gnomes” (_kumbhaṇḍa_, Sanskrit _kuṣmāṇḍa_, “pumpkin-belly”) were a race of lesser deities often depicted as pot-bellied, ugly and misshapen, though reckoned as subjects of the four great kings ([dn20:9.13]()). _Kumbha_ also means “pot” and _aṇḍa_ “testicle” ([mn56:25.4]()). Perhaps conflated with _kuṣumbha_, an insect’s venom-sack (Atharva Veda 2.32.6).
sn19.10:1.2: While the humorously painful imagery here is clear, it is less clear that the literal sense “pot-balls” was meant in general for the _kumbhaṇḍa_ as a deity. Here it is used adjectivally of a man.
